content: Recall that our abstractive model uses separate optimizers for the encoder and decoder. In Table TABREF27 we examine whether the combination of different learning rates ($\tilde{lr}_{\mathcal {E}}$ and $\tilde{lr}_{\mathcal {D}}$) is indeed beneficial. Specifically, we report model perplexity on the CNN/DailyMail validation set for varying encoder/decoder learning rates. We can see that the model performs best with $\tilde{lr}_{\mathcal {E}}=2e-3$ and $\tilde{lr}_{\mathcal {D}}=0.1$.
